correctness.rationale: The evaluation-kernel/CRT proof identifies B exactly with the product indexed by occupied Frobenius orbits; Möbius inversion counts orbits and labelled occupancy proves the formal EGF. The fixed-q,m asymptotic follows from a binomial index-two-subfield Poisson limit (even m only), ordinary pair-collision factorial moments, vanishing triple collisions, and conditional asymptotic independence. Cases m=1 and c=0 are explicit. The 16,403-array full finite checker verified all dimension, idempotent, profile and polynomial counts without using the theorem as an oracle for the algebra closure; analytic limit is separately proved.

originality.rationale: The 2010 Kravchenko–Mazur–Petrenko Theorem 6.3 counts tuples generating an entire direct power and its orbit criterion is prior; the 2020 Sercombe–Shalev paper studies full generation and generator bounds. Neither reviewed primary result states the complete all-proper-subalgebra joint Frobenius-degree isomorphism-type law or the parity-sensitive two-mode dimension-defect limit. Targeted semantic searches found no implication-equivalent claim. The novelty check is best-knowledge, with explicit priority risk.
residual_risks: An older specialized enumeration of finite-étale generated subalgebra types or an equivalent combinatorial species theorem could cover the exact EGF without using current terminology.
The independent compound-Poisson dimensional-defect law may be known in probability literature in an equivalent occupancy/subfield form; the examined primary papers do not state it.
The limit does not cover varying q or m; no independent validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The joint isomorphism-type distribution of generated unital subalgebras is an intrinsic finite-algebra statistic far richer than the previously established whole-generation flag, and the exact polynomial ranges over every q,m,r,ell. The defect law identifies and quantifies two structurally distinct sources of failed generation, including a parity-dependent field-theoretic mechanism, with nontrivial limiting distributions. These are naturally motivated by research into random generation and not arbitrary finite slices.
